resources.string: Setup and readiness

Complete basic setup, verify the bundled speech engine, then try the assistant. Android asks for ordinary permissions; special access needs the manual steps shown below. Enable optional features only when needed.

Basic setup checks to complete: %1$d. Complete them below, or continue with limited access. Optional permissions do not block this checklist.

Review setup
Basic setup checks passed. Try voice and a message to verify actual use. Optional features below may still need access.

Enable wireless debugging, pair and activate here. Readiness requires both the control service and input monitor. Automatic recovery uses the saved pairing while wireless debugging remains enabled. After force-stopping AIOS, reopen it.
Open AIOS authorization and enable the service to allow assistant actions.

In Accessibility, open AIOS screen control and enable it. This reads interface elements and enters text on foreground and virtual screens. If Android blocks the switch, review Allow restricted settings in AIOS app info first.
The switch is enabled but the accessibility service is not connected. Wait, then reopen this page. If it remains disconnected, turn AIOS screen control off and on in Accessibility.
Virtual screen prerequisites are connected. Actual creation also depends on the Android version and device implementation.
Virtual screens require both ADB activation and a connected AIOS accessibility service.
Use Request app permissions above. If Android no longer shows a prompt after denial, open App info → Permissions and allow the required access manually.

Android restricts this permission. It may require installer allowlisting or a supported default-app role; an ordinary permission dialog cannot grant it. Do not change roles for features AIOS does not implement.
Allow the corresponding foreground permission first. Then open App info → Permissions and enable background access if Android offers it. This is separate from the ordinary permission batch.
Enable Allow access to manage all files for shared-file operations when ADB is unavailable.
Enable Allow from this source for the Android installer fallback. The active ADB installation backend uses separate authorization.
Select AIOS and allow display over other apps to show the assistant panel.
Select AIOS and allow notification access to read notification events. This is separate from permission to send notifications.
Enable Allow modifying system settings for supported settings changes.
Select AIOS and enable Do Not Disturb access if you want the assistant to manage this setting.
Select AIOS and enable usage access for supported application-usage queries.
Background battery access (optional)
Find AIOS in battery optimization settings and allow unrestricted background use if needed. Manufacturer battery controls may also apply; this cannot guarantee continuous background execution.
Basic assistant setup
Optional features and shortcuts
Configure a model account. A saved account is not a successful connection test; the first message verifies credentials and network access.
Offline speech engine
Checking bundled models and running a silent decoding test. No microphone is opened and no audio is uploaded.
Bundled models loaded and decoding check passed for this language. Try a spoken message below to check the microphone. No system speech download or extra account is required.
Speech readiness has not passed. Tap to verify and prepare bundled models again. If it fails, check free storage and reopen AIOS.
Test microphone input

Tap to record for less than one second and check whether Android allows audio input. The samples are discarded, not saved or uploaded. If it fails, allow microphone permission, enable Microphone access in Quick Settings, and close other recording apps before retrying.
Try the assistant
Audio input is available and Android did not silence it during this test. Try a spoken message to verify recognition.
Testing microphone input; samples are discarded immediately.
Hide optional features
